seoTitle: Trends, Ranges & Transitions: Market Phases | LearnSMC
metaDescription: Learn how to classify bullish trends, bearish trends, consolidation ranges, and structural transitions on any timeframe before choosing setups.
quickAnswer: Markets spend their time in three structural states—bullish trends (HH/HL), bearish trends (LH/LL), and sideways ranges (EQH/EQL)—connected by brief transition phases when price closes beyond an established boundary.
takeaways: Every timeframe sits in either a trend (directional HH/HL or LH/LL), a range (contained between two boundaries), or a transition.
Range strategies fail in strong trends, and trend-continuation entries get chopped up inside tight consolidation ranges.
A transition starts with an early warning (a break of an opposing internal or external swing) and only becomes a new trend when follow-through confirms.
Always classify the higher-timeframe phase before zooming into lower-timeframe entries.

sections.title: 1. Why Market Phase Determines Which Playbook Works

blocks.text: Most trading frustration happens when a trader applies a trend-continuation rule inside a sideways box—or tries to fade range extremes during a one-way expansion. Before marking Fair Value Gaps or Order Blocks, you must answer a simpler question: is the market trending, ranging, compressing in tight consolidation, or transitioning?

Notice the practical difference between a wide Range and tight Consolidation: in a wide horizontal range (for example, $100 support to $120 resistance), traders study boundary sweeps at the edges. In a tight mid-trend consolidation (coiling inside a narrow flag), price is gathering energy and chasing mid-box swings invites whipsaw—patience for a decisive breakout close works better. Across longer cycles, these states echo Wyckoff's four stages: Accumulation (bottom range), Mark-Up (bullish trend), Distribution (top range), and Mark-Down (bearish trend).

faqs.question: How do you tell if a market is trending or ranging?
faqs.answer: Check the sequence of confirmed 3-candle swings: rising highs and rising lows (HH/HL) define an uptrend, falling highs and lows (LH/LL) define a downtrend, and overlapping swings contained between two boundaries define a range.

faqs.question: What marks a transition between a range and a trend?
faqs.answer: A transition begins when candle bodies close decisively beyond a prior range boundary or opposing swing extreme, followed by a pullback that holds rather than snapping back inside.

faqs.question: Can a market be in a range on one timeframe and a trend on another?
faqs.answer: Yes. A 15-minute chart can consolidate sideways for hours while sitting as a single pullback candle inside a bullish Daily trend.
